claims.text: The untreated material is an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with a fine dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The starting lamellar microstructure is hierarchical.
The as-cast material has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and undergoes brittle or early fracture.
The untreated alloy has strength near 1 GPa.
Annealing at approximately 800–900 °C for 2–4 hours is sub-critical for the starting alloy.
A short sub-critical anneal, optionally after moderate cold work, will partially coarsen and reconfigure the lamellar boundaries without destroying the dual-phase architecture.
Sub-critical annealing will produce refined lamellar boundaries and a precipitate dispersion.
Sub-critical annealing will relax localized stresses at internal boundaries.
Sub-critical annealing will reduce dislocation pile-ups at lamellar interfaces.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups will alleviate local stress concentrations.
Reduced boundary stress concentrations and dislocation pile-ups will diminish microcrack nucleation and delay tensile fracture.
The treatment will increase room-temperature tensile elongation by approximately 50–100% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treatment will maintain or slightly increase strength relative to the approximately 1 GPa as-cast baseline.
This alloy class remains structurally stable at operating or testing temperatures up to at least 700 °C.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration may cause excessive lamellar coarsening or degradation and thereby reduce strength.
An anneal that is too short or too cold may fail to reduce local stress concentrations sufficiently.

contradictions.description: The intervention is said to partially coarsen the lamellar boundaries, whereas the structural mediator is described as refined lamellar boundaries; the intended direction of the boundary-size change is therefore inconsistent.
